subtitle: Lesson 29 · Async Python for AI Workloads

code:
import asyncio

async def main():
    print("starting")
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    print("done")

asyncio.run(main())
caption: Creates the event loop, runs main() to completion, then closes it.

eyebrow: The event loop, in plain terms

steps.label: Another waiting coroutine runs
steps.sub: Instead of the CPU sitting idle

steps.label: The loop resumes it later
steps.sub: When its wait is actually done

code:
async def main():
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    print("2 seconds have passed")
caption: Two awaits back to back still wait fully for each — no concurrency yet.

code:
async def main():
    t1 = asyncio.create_task(asyncio.sleep(1))
    t2 = asyncio.create_task(asyncio.sleep(1))
    await t1
    await t2
    print("~1 second, not 2")
caption: Both tasks start immediately — await just waits for results already in flight.

subtitle: This exact create_task pattern, applied to real API calls.
